source.annotation: A philological study comparing Mendoza expedition diary copies, translations and related testimony. It explains why transmitted texts can offer different narratives. Its conclusions are attributed scholarly interpretations; the Atlas has not independently inspected the manuscripts.

section.title: A translated diary is not the whole record
section.text: Brian Imhoff’s comparison of copies and translations of the 1683–84 Mendoza expedition diary argues that some familiar English narratives omit conflict within the expedition. His reading includes testimony that Jumano participants defended a threatened soldier. This is an interpretation of colonial records reproduced in a modern study, not an Atlas inspection of the originals or an unmediated Jumano account. It strengthens caution about translations without resolving the historical identity debate.
